rule.description: Some names are set by birth order or circumstance: Nyandwi, Minani, Nyawenda, Bucumi (7th to 10th child), Karenzo (11th); twins Bukuru (elder) and Butoyi (younger); the child after twins Nkurikiye, Ciza or Congera. rule.description: The name is obligatory and may be accompanied by one or more given names, which then form part of the name (art. 11). The name is the one on the birth record, or the one used constantly and publicly in childhood, at least up to age 16 (art. 12). It is given by whoever declares the birth, and its choice is free (art. 13); the registrar may object only if it could harm the child (art. 14). The law sets no inheritance of the father's name

rule.description: A parent may be called 'father/mother of X' after a child (teknonymy).
